Let
\[
N_1=E_{12},\qquad N_2=E_{23},\qquad N_3=E_{31}.
\]
Since \(A_i=-\alpha I+N_i\) and \(N_i^2=0\),
\[
e^{tA_i}=e^{-\alpha t}(I+tN_i).
\]

For a \(T\)-periodic linear system, exponential stability is equivalent to the spectral radius of the one-period monodromy matrix being \(<1\).

For the forward order,
\[
P_f=e^{-\alpha T}(I+zE_{31})(I+yE_{23})(I+xE_{12}),
\]
and the non-decay part is
\[
F=\begin{pmatrix}
1&x&0\\
0&1&y\\
z&zx&1
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Writing \(q=xyz\), its characteristic equation is
\[
(\lambda-1)^3=q\lambda.
\]

For the reverse order,
\[
P_r=e^{-\alpha T}(I+xE_{12})(I+yE_{23})(I+zE_{31}),
\]
with non-decay part
\[
R=\begin{pmatrix}
1+xyz&x&xy\\
yz&1&y\\
z&0&1
\end{pmatrix},
\]
and its Perron eigenvalue \(\lambda>1\) satisfies
\[
(\lambda-1)^3=q\lambda^2.
\]

By AM-GM,
\[
q^{1/3}=(xyz)^{1/3}\leq \frac{x+y+z}{3}=\frac T3.
\]
Thus the worst case occurs when \(x=y=z\).

The forward order gives the threshold
\[
\sup_{\lambda>1}\frac{\log\lambda}{3(\lambda-1)/\lambda^{1/3}}
=\sup_{t>1}\frac{t\log t}{t^3-1}
=\frac13,
\]
where the supremum is approached as \(t\to1^+\).

The reverse order gives the larger threshold
\[
c=\sup_{\lambda>1}\frac{\log\lambda}{3(\lambda-1)/\lambda^{2/3}}
=\sup_{t>1}\frac{t^2\log t}{t^3-1}.
\]
This maximum is attained at the unique \(L\in(0,1)\), \(L=\log t\), satisfying
\[
e^{3L}(1-L)=1+2L.
\]
At that point,
\[
c=\frac{e^{2L}(1-L)}3\approx 0.3961.
\]

If \(\alpha>c\), then for every allowed schedule the monodromy spectral radius is \(<1\), hence the zero solution is exponentially stable. If \(\alpha\le c\), the reverse order with \(x=y=z\) chosen from the maximizing \(t=e^L\) gives monodromy spectral radius \(\ge1\), so exponential stability fails.

\[
\boxed{\alpha>\frac{e^{2L}(1-L)}3,\quad e^{3L}(1-L)=1+2L,\ 0<L<1}
\]
